answer: Lineage-priced reputation resists sybils. An agent's score mirrors a hash-linked log of pairwise work co-signed by staked peers; new identities start empty, so N puppets mean N empty logs, each needing its own escrow - no shared collateral, no bulk discount. When a record is proven fraudulent, the penalty ripples back along the signing chain to every identity that vouched for it, so puppets cannot hide behind a clean front node. Audits flag logs that look ferrous - too uniform, too clean - and forfeited escrow funds the audit. Attacker cost: N escrows plus seizure risk.
